title: Воспоминание о первой встрече с Кристиной  (Flashback to First Meeting Kristina)

segments.t: In the flashback, while Kristina was still working as a hostess before marrying Nagiyev, Chef Barinov spots her in the dining room and crudely brags to the cooks about wanting to seduce her. Seconds later, restaurant owner Dmitry Nagiyev walks over and warmly greets Kristina right in front of the stunned Chef.
Быстро на своё место встречать гостей.
Я тоже рад вас видеть, Кристина.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'All right, Ilya, stop laughing.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'like this' before landing on 'to laugh loudly'.
'Where is Kristina supposed to be?' Kristina anchors the line on 'Kristina', while 'maybe' completes the thought.
Быстро на своё место встречать гостей.
'Get back to your post quickly to greet the guests.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'quickly' and finishing on 'guests'. Dmitry answers right away.
'Girls, look alive, hurry up.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'girls' and 'living' in a few short words.
'We will do it ourselves.' The meaning hinges on 'yourself' working together with 'we'll do' in spoken Russian.
'Good afternoon.' Notice how Russian expresses 'good' and 'day' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Dmitry answers right away.
'I would definitely take her for a spin.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'to deep-fry' without extra filler words.
'I would take her for a spin too.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'to deep-fry'.
'Except she is a high-flying bird.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'only' before landing on 'bird'. Dmitry answers right away.
'To her, we are nobodies.' The grammar packs 'we' and 'nobody' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Listen, who even are you?' Kristina raises the pitch on 'at all' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'Hello, Dmitry Vladimirovich.' Ilya brings out the contrast between 'hello' and 'Dmitry' in a few short words. Dmitry answers right away.
Я тоже рад вас видеть, Кристина.
'I am glad to see you too, Kristina.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'Kristina' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Быстро на своё место встречать гостей.
Я тоже рад вас видеть, Кристина.
